reason: S1 exposes the new production API meshopt_remesh, but no H0 harness invokes it. Its mesh-index and vertex-buffer inputs plus resolution, stride, capacity, and options parameters define a distinct fuzz-worthy input protocol that the existing meshlet, codec, and simplification calls do not exercise.
evidence: src/meshoptimizer.h declares meshopt_remesh(float* destination, size_t max_triangle_count, const unsigned int* indices, size_t index_count, const float* vertex_positions, size_t vertex_count, size_t vertex_positions_stride, int resolution, unsigned int options).
src/remesher.cpp enforces meshopt_remesh-specific boundaries: index_count % 3 == 0, vertex_positions_stride between 12 and 256 and divisible by sizeof(float), and resolution between 1 and 250.
tools/simplifyfuzz.cpp invokes meshopt_simplify, meshopt_simplifyWithAttributes, and meshopt_simplifyWithUpdate, but not meshopt_remesh; the other H0 paths also contain no meshopt_remesh call.
recommended_action: Add a meshopt_remesh fuzz path that derives valid triangle indices and vertex positions from fuzzer bytes, allocates destination according to varied max_triangle_count values, and varies resolution across its valid boundary values, vertex_positions_stride, options, mesh sizes, and degenerate geometry.
